rule: Every head is built on a circle for the cranium; the face hangs below it and the skull above the brows stays a smooth round dome, the same for every character type.
check: Is the cranium above the brow line a smooth, round dome with no flattening or bumps?

rule: Split the lower half of the skull circle into four equal bands: brows sit on the first line (1/8 of the diameter below the circle's centre), the upper lash line on the second, and the bottom of the iris reaches the third.
check: Do the brows sit only slightly below the vertical middle of the cranium circle, with the upper lash line one similar step lower?

rule: For a teen the eyes occupy the lower quarter of the skull circle (between 1/8 and 3/8 of the diameter below its centre), so the forehead and cranium make up well over half the head height.
check: Is the vertical distance from the top of the skull to the brows larger than the distance from the brows to the chin?

rule: For teens the chin tip lies about 1/4 of the skull-circle diameter below the circle's bottom; the whole face below the nose is short.
check: Is the distance from the nose to the chin tip short, roughly a quarter of the cranium width?

rule: The teen jaw lines leave the skull circle near the brow line and run in nearly straight diagonals to a soft point at the chin, making a pentagon-like lower face (no rounded bulging cheeks).
check: Do the jaw contours run in nearly straight lines from the cheek to a softly pointed chin?

rule: The outer ends of the upper lash lines touch the sides of the skull circle, so the face at eye level is as wide as the cranium.
check: Do the outer corners of the eyes sit close to the side contour of the face, leaving only a thin strip of cheek outside them?

rule: The top of the hair sits about 1/4 of the circle diameter above the skull; manga heads are top heavy, which reads as youthful.
check: Does the hair mass rise clearly above the skull so the head looks top heavy?

rule: In 3/4 view a gently curved centre line runs from the chin tip up to the brow line, set off toward the far side; the far contour follows the circle down to about the brow line, then the cheek/jaw angles in to the chin.
check: In 3/4, does the far side of the face show a cheek contour that turns inward below the eye toward the chin?

rule: In 3/4 view the brows, eyes, nose and mouth all touch the curved centre line at different points; the far eye sits between that line and the far contour.
check: In 3/4, are the nose and mouth placed on a curving centre line that sits well toward the far side of the face?

rule: In profile the face line leaves the skull circle between bands 2 and 3, slopes straight to a nose tip just above the circle bottom, then drops to the chin with two small lip bumps midway; the jaw line points back toward the bottom of the vertical centre line without reaching it.
check: In profile, is the brow-to-nose contour a straight slope with a small pointed nose, followed by small lip bumps and a pointed chin?

rule: In profile the back of the neck joins just behind the ear, and the throat line starts halfway between the chin tip and the bottom of the vertical centre line.
check: In profile, does the throat start about halfway back along the underside of the jaw, rather than right at the chin?

rule: As eyes get bigger the nose and mouth must get smaller and simpler; big eyes with a realistic nose and mouth breaks the style.
check: Are the nose and mouth small and simplified in proportion to the large eyes?

rule: Ear height tracks stylisation: realistic faces have ears level with the eyes, very cartoony faces have them level with the nose.
check: Do the ears sit roughly between eye level and nose level, matching a mid-cartoony style (not floating above the eyes)?

rule: In the slightly cartoony (boys' action) style the eyes grow but the eye-to-nose-tip distance stays close to real anatomy; in very cartoony styles the eyes swallow that gap.
check: Is there visible skin between the bottom of the eyes and the nose tip (the nose is not touching the eye line)?

rule: In the most cartoony (shojo) style the eyes are very large and the brows sit very high, near the circle's centre line or above.
check: For a large-eyed shojo variant, do the brows sit well above the eyes with clear forehead skin between them?

rule: Manga teen boys and girls share almost the same face structure; gender reads mainly through hair and a slightly thinner upper lash line on boys.
check: Apart from hair and lash thickness, do the male and female heads share the same jaw, eye placement and proportions?

rule: The male upper lash line is a little thinner than the female one and lacks the female's flicked lash tick at the outer corner.
check: On the male head, is the upper lash line thinner and less flared than on the female head?

rule: A boy's neck is drawn thicker than a girl's and its sides start closer to the jaw corners.
check: On the male head, is the neck noticeably wider than the female neck, starting near the jaw corners?

rule: A long-haired male needs a thicker neck and more angular facial features to avoid reading as female.
check: If the male has long hair, are the jaw and brows more angular and the neck thicker than the female's?

rule: Adults have a longer lower face: the chin is about 1/3 of the circle diameter below the circle, and the cheek/jaw outline is squarer and more complex.
check: For an adult variant, is the lower face visibly longer and the jaw squarer than on the teen head?

rule: On adults the brows and eyes sit one full band higher than on teens, and the eyes are smaller and narrower.
check: For an adult variant, are the eyes smaller and set higher relative to the chin than on the teen?

rule: The biggest young-versus-old difference is the nose: adults get a fully drawn nose with a bridge line and nostril wings, teens only a tiny mark.
check: Does the teen nose stay a tiny minimal form, while any adult variant has a fuller bridge and nostrils?

rule: Age is shown with few lines: crow's-feet, one line under each eye, and lines beside the mouth; a single line under each eye plus cheekbone lines suggests a mature but not old man.
check: For a youthful head, is the face free of under-eye lines, crow's-feet and mouth-side creases?

rule: Lines at the mouth sides add age, so keep the area around eyes and mouth clean on characters meant to look young; mothers get only subtle lines.
check: Is the skin around the mouth and eyes clean of creases or crease-like shading?

rule: Adult (father-type) eyes are narrow almonds about 2.5 times wider than tall with small irises, under thick, straight brows set close to the eye.
check: For an adult male variant, are the eyes narrow almonds under thick, low, straight brows?

rule: Adult mouths add a short line under the mouth for the lower lip; youthful mouths are a single short line.
check: Is the teen mouth a single simple line or crease, without a separate lower-lip contour?

rule: Elderly faces add crow's-feet fanning from the outer eyes, cheekbone lines, short choppy lines at the lips, forehead lines and neck creases; villains get a prominent nose, sunken cheeks and a scowl.
check: For an elderly variant, are there wrinkles at the outer eyes, cheekbones and lips?

rule: A fuller-figured face replaces the pointed chin with a rounded U-shaped bottom, keeps all features in the standard positions, and may add a curved double-chin line.
check: For a fuller variant, is the chin rounded instead of pointed, with the eyes, nose and mouth in standard positions?

rule: Fuller-figured characters get a much wider neck than the standard manga neck.
check: For a fuller variant, is the neck nearly as wide as the jaw?

rule: In a fuller 3/4 face the features sit as usual but the space from mouth to chin outline is clearly larger, and a short line at the ear base marks the cheek edge.
check: For a fuller variant in 3/4, is there a larger gap between the mouth and the chin outline than on the standard head?

rule: For a child divide the lower half of the circle into three (brows on line 1, lashes on line 2); the eyes are nearly twice as big as a teen's and round.
check: For a child variant, are the eyes much larger and rounder than the teen's, filling more of the face?

rule: A child's jaw still ends in a blunt point, but the cheeks are squared off, running almost straight down from the skull before angling in, for a baby-faced look.
check: For a child variant, do the cheeks drop almost vertically before turning in to a short, blunt chin?

rule: On the child the mouth is halfway between the bottom of the skull circle and the chin tip, the same rule as for teens.
check: Is the mouth about halfway between the nose and the chin tip?

rule: A child profile has a tiny nose point at the circle-bottom level and a short, straight drop to the chin; the underside of the jaw stays mostly horizontal and never touches the circle.
check: For a child in profile, is the nose a tiny point and the jaw underside nearly horizontal?

rule: Child ears can be made slightly larger than a teen's for extra cuteness.
check: For a child variant, are the ears equal to or slightly larger than the teen's relative to the head?

rule: The basic teen eye fits a box slightly taller than wide, with one box-width of space between the two eyes.
check: Is each eye about as tall as it is wide, or slightly taller?

rule: Leave exactly one eye width of empty skin between the eyes; that gap matters as much as the eye shapes.
check: Is the gap between the inner eye corners about one eye width?

rule: Brows and both lash lines tilt up slightly toward the centre of the face; the upper lash curve is stronger than the lower.
check: Do the upper lash lines rise slightly from the outer corners toward the nose, with a stronger curve than the lower lash line?

rule: The upper lash line is the heaviest, darkest mark on the face, thickest across the top and flicking out at the outer corner; the lower lash is a thin, short stroke that does not run the full width.
check: Is the upper lash line clearly thicker and darker than the lower lash line, and does the lower line stop short of the full eye width?

rule: The iris is a tall oval filling most of the eye height, with a smaller oval pupil nested inside; its bottom flattens slightly where it meets the lower lash line.
check: Is the iris a tall oval that runs nearly from the upper lash to the lower lash and is cut off slightly at the bottom?

rule: In a neutral eye the top of the iris tucks under the upper lash line; white shows only at the sides of the iris, not above it.
check: In the neutral face, does the upper lid overlap the top of the iris with no white showing above it?

rule: Each iris gets a small white circular highlight near the top, overlapping the iris edge, on the same side in both eyes.
check: Does each iris have a small white highlight near its top, on the same side in both eyes?

rule: Most manga eyes have at least one highlight; it can sit at the top of the iris, the bottom, or both, and a single dot can be enough.
check: Does each eye show at least one clear specular highlight?

rule: Irises are darker at the top and lighter toward the bottom (in ink, denser hatching at the top, under the upper lid).
check: Is each iris darker at the top, under the lid, and lighter toward the bottom?

rule: The upper eyelid fold is a short curved line above the inner part of the eye only, not across the full width as in real life.
check: Is the eyelid crease a short line over the inner half of the eye rather than running across the whole lid?

rule: In 3/4 view the far eye is compressed horizontally (narrower than the near eye) and sits against the far cheek contour, with a small sliver of skin outside it.
check: In 3/4, is the far eye narrower than the near eye, with only a small strip of face outside it?

rule: In profile the eye is a narrow wedge, roughly a third as wide as the front eye, lying between bands 2 and 3, close to but not touching the face contour, with the iris as a thin vertical ellipse at its front.
check: In profile, is the eye a narrow wedge set just behind the face contour, not a full almond?

rule: Semirealistic manga eyes are small and narrow, closer to anatomy; cartoony eyes are big, round, and simple; shojo eyes become huge with several highlights and lashes.
check: Is the eye size consistent with one chosen style (not a mix, such as huge irises inside narrow realistic lids)?

rule: Shrinking the iris far down makes a character look menacing or shifty; pupil-less irises give a glassy look. Use these only on purpose.
check: In the neutral expression, is the iris large (not a tiny dot floating in white)?

rule: Female upper lashes end in one or two small flicked ticks at the outer corner; the lash line is thick and dark.
check: On the female head, does the upper lash line end in a small outward flick or tick at the outer corner?

rule: Teen brows are thin, gently arched single strokes, a little longer than the eye, sitting about one band (1/8 of the skull diameter) above the upper lash line.
check: Are the brows thin, gently curved strokes, slightly longer than the eye, with a clear gap above the lash line?

rule: In 3/4 view the far brow is not directly above the far eye; it shifts a little toward the centre line.
check: In 3/4, is the far brow shifted toward the centre of the face relative to the far eye, rather than centred over it?

rule: Male brows are slightly thicker and straighter than female brows and sit at the same height.
check: On the male head, are the brows a little thicker and flatter than on the female head?

rule: Brows carry most of each expression: their tilt, how close they sit to the lashes, and any crook or zigzag change the emotion more than any other feature.
check: In the expression set, does each emotion use a clearly different brow tilt or brow shape?

rule: The teen nose rests on the bottom of the skull circle on the centre line; it is a tiny mark (a short hook or small shadow tick), not a full form.
check: Is the nose a small, minimal form on the face centre line, sitting a little below the bottom of the eyes?

rule: In 3/4 view the nose is a small angled hook that pokes past the centre line toward the far side, with its tip at the circle-bottom level.
check: In 3/4, does the nose tip project slightly beyond the face centre line toward the far side?

rule: In profile the nose is a small sharp point with a straight upper slope and a short concave underside back to the lip.
check: In profile, is the nose a small sharp point with a straight bridge?

rule: In an adult 3/4 face the nose tip lies between bands 3 and 4 at the circle edge, drawn with a long bridge line and an angular underside.
check: For an adult in 3/4, does the nose show a longer bridge and an angular underside instead of a tiny dot?

rule: The mouth sits midway between the bottom of the skull circle (nose level) and the chin tip.
check: Is the mouth about halfway between the nose and the chin tip?

rule: The neutral teen mouth is a short, slightly upturned line, roughly one eye width long, narrower than the gap between the eyes.
check: Is the closed mouth a short line no wider than about one eye width?

rule: In 3/4 view the mouth starts at the centre line and extends mainly toward the near side.
check: In 3/4, does the mouth extend mainly to the near side of the face centre line?

rule: In profile the mouth is a short stroke set back from the lip bumps, about midway between nose and chin.
check: In profile, is the mouth a short line set back from the lip contour, halfway between nose and chin?

rule: Open mouths are simple rounded shapes (lens, oval or D) filled with one flat interior tone; there is no lip modelling.
check: When the mouth opens, is the interior one flat colour with a simple rounded outline and no lip volume?

rule: A big smile opens as a D or half-moon: a nearly straight or slightly curved top edge and a deep curved bottom, wider than the closed mouth.
check: In the big smile, is the open mouth a D or half-moon with a flat top and a curved bottom?

rule: Teeth show as a single white upper band along the top of the open mouth, sometimes with one small fang point; lower teeth are usually left out.
check: When teeth show, are they a single white upper band (perhaps with a small fang), with no individual teeth drawn?

rule: Clenched teeth are a white rectangle-like shape whose outline has a break in it, sometimes with a horizontal line between upper and lower teeth.
check: In the determined expression, does the mouth show clenched white teeth framed by an outline?

rule: When a tongue shows in a wide laughing mouth it is a simple lighter rounded shape at the bottom of the mouth, never detailed.
check: If a tongue is visible, is it a simple rounded lighter shape in the lower mouth, without detail?

rule: The top of the ear is level with the middle of the eye and its bottom sits just above the mouth line.
check: Does the top of the ear line up with the middle of the eye and its bottom sit just above the mouth?

rule: Ears are simple C shapes with one or two inner curves; they stick out modestly from the sides of the head.
check: Are the ears simple C shapes with one or two inner curves, sticking out only modestly?

rule: In 3/4 view only the near ear shows; the far ear is hidden behind the skull.
check: In 3/4, is the far ear hidden?

rule: In profile the ear sits between bands 2 and 4, its front edge flat against the vertical centre line of the skull circle.
check: In profile, is the ear placed at the middle of the head (front to back), spanning from eye level to just below nose level?

rule: The teen neck is a pair of nearly straight lines starting inside the jaw, about half the face width at ear level; it widens into the shoulders with long diagonals.
check: Is the neck about half as wide as the face at ear level?

rule: In 3/4 view the neck meets the ear/cheek junction on one side and the chin tip on the other.
check: In 3/4, does the near neck line start under the ear and the front neck line start close to the chin?

rule: Every finished head gets a shadow under the chin: a band on the neck that follows the jaw shape, darkest right under the jaw.
check: Is there a clear cast shadow on the neck right under the jaw, following the jaw's shape?

rule: Hair strand lines curve along the shape of the skull, and the hair silhouette stands off the skull rather than being painted on it.
check: Do the hair strands curve with the head shape, with the hair sitting visibly off the scalp?

rule: Bangs are arranged to part over the forehead so they don't hide the eyes; they reach about to the brows.
check: Do the bangs leave both eyes fully visible while reaching about down to the brows?

rule: There is real distance between the hairline/outer hair and the actual skull; if the hair hugs the skull the head looks wrong.
check: Does the hair volume extend clearly beyond the skull outline at the top and sides?

rule: A comparatively short haircut makes a character read as male; short hair on girls suggests innocence, long straight hair a more worldly character.
check: Does the hairstyle match the intended gender read (shorter for the default male)?

rule: Long side locks drop in front of or beside the ears, framing the cheeks and leaving the jaw outline readable.
check: Do side locks frame the cheeks without hiding the jaw outline and chin?

rule: Older characters get a larger forehead and calmer, less flashy hairstyles.
check: For an adult variant, is more forehead showing and is the hairstyle simpler than the teen's?

rule: In colour the face is flat skin, and the hair carries a lighter highlight band across the crown.
check: Is the facial skin nearly flat-shaded while the hair shows a distinct lighter highlight band across the crown?

rule: Children (and happy chibis) get soft pink blush ovals on the outer cheeks just below the eyes.
check: For a child variant, are there soft pink blush spots on the cheeks just below the outer eyes?

rule: The cheerful default: a small, gentle curved smile, with the lower edge of the eyes flattened as if the cheeks were rising.
check: In the happy expression, is the smile small and gentle, and is the lower edge of each eye flattened upward?

rule: Ecstatic joy: eyes squeezed shut into upward-bowed arcs (like ^ shapes), a big open D-shaped mouth, and blush strokes across the cheeks; the bottom of the mouth may be left open.
check: In the laughing expression, are the eyes closed upward arcs and the mouth a large open D shape?

rule: Big happiness and embarrassment add diagonal blush hatching or a pink flush across the cheeks under the eyes.
check: In the laughing expression, is there blush on the cheeks below the eyes?

rule: Confusion is shown mainly by asymmetric brows: one lowered and angled like anger, the other raised high; the mouth is a tiny 'o'.
check: In the confused expression, is one brow lowered and the other raised, with a small round mouth?

rule: Concern/serious: brows slightly curved and angled a bit down toward the centre, with only a hint of a furrow, and a mid-size open mouth.
check: In the serious/concerned expression, do the brows angle slightly down toward the nose without a strong crook?

rule: Sadness or regret: brows follow a crooked path, rising toward the centre of the forehead; upper lids are heavy, and the mouth is a tiny frown.
check: In the sad expression, do the inner ends of the brows rise toward the centre, with heavy upper lids and a small frown?

rule: Crying sadness: big irises tucked well under the upper lids, one or two tears (not floods), and a mouth with a wavering lower lip.
check: In the crying expression, are the irises large and tucked under the lids, with only one or two tears and a wobbly lower lip?

rule: Boredom: flatten the upper lash line and tuck the iris at least halfway beneath it; brows float at a neutral angle; the mouth is small and closed.
check: In the bored expression, do flat upper lids cover at least half of each iris, with neutral brows and a small closed mouth?

rule: Determination: brows angled steeply down toward the nose and pressed very close to the upper lashes, with clenched teeth.
check: In the determined expression, are the brows angled down toward the nose and almost touching the upper lash lines?

rule: Anger: like determination, plus extra crooks (zigzags) at the ends of the brows, furrow marks between them, and a wide-open mouth with bared upper teeth.
check: In the angry expression, do the brows angle down with a crook near the inner ends, and is the mouth wide open showing upper teeth?

rule: In anger and determination the eye highlights shrink or vanish and the upper lid flattens over the iris.
check: In the angry expression, are the eye highlights reduced or gone and the upper lids flattened?

rule: Distress: brows curve upward, at least one ending in a zigzag for a furrowed brow; the irises do not quite touch the upper lids; tears bead at the lower lids, and there is blush.
check: In the distressed expression, are the brows raised with a zigzag, with white visible between iris and upper lid?

rule: Surprise: small irises float inside the whites (white visible all round), with a small open gasping mouth and raised brows.
check: In the surprised expression, are the irises small with white showing above and below, and is the mouth a small open oval?

rule: Embarrassment: apologetic upturned brows plus a big open smile, wide-open eyes and heavy blush across the nose and both cheeks.
check: In the embarrassed expression, are the brows tilted up at the inner ends while the mouth smiles widely and the cheeks blush?

rule: A comic embarrassed variant squeezes the eyes into > < chevrons over a toothy grin with blush hatching.
check: In the embarrassed variant, are the eyes squeezed into > < chevrons with blush and a grin?

rule: Comic shock turns the eyes into heavily outlined white circles with tiny or no pupils, a huge open mouth reaching toward the chin, and vertical gloom lines under the eyes.
check: In the shocked variant, are the eyes blank white circles with tiny or no pupils and the mouth very large?

rule: Fright adds vertical lines across the upper face (never crossing the eyes), small irises without highlights, and a tiny 'o' mouth.
check: In the scared expression, are the irises small and the mouth a tiny 'o', with any vertical gloom lines kept off the eyes?

rule: Chibi rage uses slanted brows (one with a zigzag crook), white circle eyes tucked under the brows, a bellowing mouth reaching the bottom of the head, and a cross-shaped popping vein; any shading lines must keep the eyes pure white.
check: In the furious variant, are the eyes left bright white under steeply slanted brows, with a cross-shaped anger vein?

rule: A wink closes one eye into a downward-bowed arc while the other stays fully open, paired with an open smile.
check: In the wink, is one eye a closed arc while the other is fully open?

rule: Disapproval/pout: half-lidded eyes with flat upper lids, brows angled down, a small pouting frown and light blush.
check: In the disapproving expression, are the lids half closed over the irises with a small pout?

rule: Despondent wailing: eyes squeezed shut with tears streaming, a wobbly open wailing mouth, and tear drops flying from the face.
check: In the wailing variant, are the eyes squeezed shut with streaming tears and the mouth a wobbly open shape?

rule: Frustration: eyes squeezed shut as downward chevrons under lowered brows, a small tight mouth, and a sweat drop.
check: In the frustrated expression, are the eyes squeezed shut under lowered brows with a small tight mouth?

rule: Devious: eyes narrowed to slanted slits under down-angled brows, with a wide closed or toothy grin.
check: In the devious expression, are the eyes narrow slanted slits with a wide grin?

rule: An 'in love' chibi swaps the irises for heart shapes and pairs them with a big open smile.
check: In the in-love variant, are the irises replaced by hearts?

rule: Shy/meek: blank eyes with dot pupils, a small round mouth and a still face.
check: In the shy variant, are the eyes simplified with small dot pupils and the mouth a tiny circle?

rule: Tears are drawn as bead or droplet shapes pooling at the lower lid's outer part and running down the cheek, with a highlight; one or two only.
check: When tears appear, are they one or two glossy droplets at the lower lid or cheek, not a continuous sheet?

rule: Panels play off a neutral, innocent face against a strongly changed reaction face; the neutral must be calm (relaxed brows, closed small mouth) so the change reads.
check: Is the neutral face calm, with relaxed level brows and a small closed mouth, so that every other expression differs clearly from it?

rule: Many expressions (confusion, distress, wink) work through deliberate left/right asymmetry of brows or eyes, while basic happy, sad and angry stay roughly symmetrical.
check: Do the asymmetric expressions (confused, wink) actually differ between left and right while the basic emotions stay symmetrical?
